steps.body: Two angles that fit together into a **square corner** are **complementary**: they add to **90°**. Two angles that fit along a **straight line** are **supplementary**: they add to **180°**.
steps.narration: Two angles that fit together into a **square corner** are **complementary**: they add to **90°**. Two angles that fit along a **straight line** are **supplementary**: they add to **180°**.

widget.prompt: One angle is 35°. Open the other until the two complete a right angle.
widget.successFeedback: 55°, because 35 + 55 = 90. Complementary means 'completes the square corner' — and once you see the corner, you never need to recall which word means 90 and which means 180.
widget.lowFeedback: The two angles do not reach a right angle yet.
widget.highFeedback: The two angles have opened past a right angle.

predict.prompt: One angle is 35°. Its complement — together they square off a right angle — measures…
predict.reveal: Complements complete 90°: the partner is 90 − 35 = 55°. Answering 145° completes a straight line instead — that's the supplement, the other half of the C/S trap.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents complementary.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for complementary must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines complementary.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

steps.body: A memory hook: **C**omplementary makes a **C**orner (90°); **S**upplementary makes a **S**traight line (180°). To find a missing partner, subtract the known angle from the pair's total.
steps.narration: A memory hook: **C**omplementary makes a **C**orner (90°); **S**upplementary makes a **S**traight line (180°). To find a missing partner, subtract the known angle from the pair's total.

widget.prompt: Two angles are supplementary. One is 110°. What is the other, in degrees?

commonErrors.feedback: You may have subtracted from 130 — supplementary uses 180°: 180 − 110 = 70.

widget.prompt: Two angles are complementary. One is 62°. What is the other, in degrees?
Sort each angle pair by its type.

items.label: 40° and 50°
items.feedback: 40 + 50 = 90 — they fit a square corner, so complementary.

items.label: 100° and 80°
items.feedback: 100 + 80 = 180 — they fill a straight line, so supplementary.

widget.missFeedback: Not quite — add each pair: 90° means complementary, 180° means supplementary.
widget.successFeedback: All sorted — corners hold 90°, straight lines hold 180°.

explanationVariants: Two complementary angles share only 90°, so neither can be 90° or more.
Each complementary angle must be under 90°, since the pair totals 90°.

widget.prompt: Why can't an angle of 95° have a complement?

options.label: A 90° total is already less than 95°.
options.feedback: Correct — a positive partner cannot reduce 95° to the complementary total of 90°.

options.label: A complement must match the given angle.
options.feedback: Complementary angles need not match; their measures must add to 90°.

options.label: Only even angles can have complements.
options.feedback: Parity is irrelevant; any positive angle below 90° has a complement.

widget.prompt: Three angles fit together into a square corner. Two of them are 25° and 40°. What is the third, in degrees?

commonErrors.feedback: That used 180° — a square corner holds 90°: 90 − 25 − 40 = 25.
That's just the two known angles combined — subtract from 90: 25.

hints: A square corner holds 90° in total.

steps.body: Complementary pairs total 90° (a corner); supplementary pairs total 180° (a straight line).
takeaways: Complementary: adds to 90°. Supplementary: adds to 180°.
